search_log: Searched "The Armor of Light" Ken Follett excerpt, first chapter, publisher, and author-site combinations.
Searched both US "Armor" and UK "Armour" spellings with point of view, third-person, omniscient narrator, and narration perspective terms.
Opened the sustained Scroll book excerpt and the Historical Novel Society review used as evidence.
Checked Penguin Random House and Google Books pages; their accessible text provided catalog copy rather than readable narrative prose.
Checked an Orange County Library/OverDrive result, but the excerpt page returned an access error; also found duplicative opening samples and lower-authority uploads that were not needed.
person_note: The book uses nonparticipating third-person narration, moving among many characters with omniscient access to their thoughts and feelings. Several interior Goodreads passages show the same external narrating stance, while dialogue, speech, fragments, and the clipped final quote were not treated as competing narrator voices. The authorized opening excerpt independently demonstrates third-person narration, and the whole-book Historical Novel Society review explicitly identifies the omniscient narrator. The opening alone would have limited scope, but the whole-book description and interior quote pattern resolve that limitation; no credible first- or second-person base section was found.
